messages:
cheng: Heads up — I’m seeing a regression after the shared-mem tiling change landed this morning. Fused Flash + paged-attention path on 13B, seq=4096 is ~20-25% slower than before. perf-bot posted the snapshot below.

perf-bot: [regression-detector] detected throughput drop on fused_flash_paged (13B) at 2026-03-16T22:15Z. throughput: 1870 tok/s -> 1450 tok/s (-22%), p50 latency +30%. dashboard: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/176341

sandeep: Can you paste the exact bench command and kernel flags? My gut says occupancy dropped after the tiling change.

cheng: Sure — ran this on a single A100-40G dev node:

```
python -m rwd.perf.attn_bench \ 
  --model gpt-13b \ 
  --seq 4096 \ 
  --batch 1 \ 
  --kv-mode paged \ 
  --kernel fused_flash \ 
  --tiling 64x32 \ 
  --pipeline-stages 2 \ 
  --ctas-per-sm 4
```

nvprof / nsight excerpt: (truncated)
```
Memory Bandwidth: peak 820.3 GB/s, avg 640.1 GB/s
SM Occupancy: 0.41
L2 Read BW: 340 GB/s
DRAM Reads (paged misses): increased by 2.8x vs baseline
```

maria: Paging the KV cache will blow up DRAM reads when misses cascade at long seqs — that plus the smaller tiling (64x32) might be increasing global memory pressure. Two quick ideas: prefetch multiple page entries per request or increase pipeline stages to hide page load latency.

kevin: Quick experiment proposal: try tiling 128x16 and pipeline-stages=3, increase ctas-per-sm to 6. Larger tile reduces sharedmem per-warp overhead and might improve coalescing. Example tweak:

```
--tiling 128x16 --pipeline-stages 3 --ctas-per-sm 6
```

eli: Ran kevin's tweak on my dev rig (A100-80GB sim) for short smoke: throughput +12% vs the bad run, peak BW down to 735 GB/s, occupancy up to 0.55. Still not at the pre-change baseline but moving in the right direction.

sandeep: Good. Next steps: 1) run a microbench that disables paged KV misses (force hits) to separate kernel compute vs paging overhead, 2) bisect the tiling change commits to find the regression point, 3) run a variant where we increase sharedmem split so per-thread smem usage drops. I'll open a tiny PR to add an opt-in smem-split flag and a microbench harness.

cheng: Sounds good. I’ll attach the full perf logs and the perf-bot link to the bisect issue. If the microbench shows compute regression even with perfect KV hits then we need to revisit kernel launch policy (ctas/threads) or the new kernel math.

kevin: I’ll also try a fused-attn-only run (no paged, no fusion) to sanity-check kernel math. If fused_flash itself regresses, we should revert tiling change for the fused path only. :thumbsup:
